basis: Independent observation of each original PNG opened once, at original detail. No prior modern figure or answer used to establish geometry.

facts: One subfigure. Top path from left vertical outer wire through a blank circular meter to one horizontal rectangular series resistor and then the right outer wire. The circle has no interior letter or needle. R_internal is above/right of the meter, R_added above the resistor.

Left and right outer wires extend to filled bottom junctions and short outside terminal leads. Between these nodes is a large lower rectangle whose interior says measured voltage. This block is not a second resistor symbol.

A thin vertical guide descends from the meter/resistor intermediate wire to the first voltage span. The first span has two separate outward-headed intervals: V0 over the meter from the left wire to the divider, and V_added over the resistor from the divider to the right wire.
A second, lower outward-headed span labelled V reaches from the left outer wire to the right outer wire. It is a voltage annotation, not an additional conducting path.
Six dimension-arrow heads total: two for V0, two for V_added, two for V. No numerical resistance, voltage, current or length value is printed in the image. No scale/grid or additional apparatus.

facts: One subfigure. Two filled lower junctions connect a main horizontal wire, with incoming and outgoing terminal leads. One rectangular shunt resistor lies between the lower junctions.

An upper parallel branch rises vertically at the left junction, runs right through one circular ammeter marked A, and descends vertically to the right junction. The ammeter internal resistance label Ra is below the circle.

Current I enters on the lower-left lead and leaves on the lower-right lead, both rightward. The shunt current is rightward on the lower-left and lower-right wires around the resistor; I_shunt is printed below the lower-left branch wire.
Meter current I0 is shown upward on the left upright, with a label immediately to its right. Small rightward arrow heads occur in each upper horizontal lead, to the left and right of the circle.

R_shunt is printed above the lower resistor. Seven current arrows total: input, output, two shunt arrows, upward meter arrow, two upper-lead arrows. No numbers, needle, scale, battery, switch, extra resistor or voltage meter.

facts: One subfigure with four rectangular resistor symbols. Main horizontal conducting path is A--r1--B--r2--r3--C--D. No branch leaves the unlabelled connection between r2 and r3.
A lower branch descends at B, runs through r4, then rises at C. It bypasses r2 and r3 together, not r1. C--D is an ideal wire in the stem's model, not another resistor.

A, B, C, D are four distinct filled marked points. A and D labels are below the main wire; B and C labels are above it. r1,r2,r3 labels are below the main resistor rectangles, and r4 is below the lower resistor.
The upper horizontal outward-headed span V goes between upright endpoint guides at A and D. Its two opposing arrow heads indicate terminal voltage, not a conducting bypass or current direction.

All resistor labels are symbolic; the source image has no numeric ohm, volt, current, power or dimension values. A tiny isolated diagonal scan mark above r3 is not a component, a node, a current arrow or an interpreted label.
